newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to declare some Danish shipbuilding aid illegal.
newsitem.headline: EU to declare some Danish shipbuilding aid illegal.

text.p: The European Commission will rule on Wednesday that illegal state aid was granted to a shipyard which is part of Danish shipping and energy group A.P. Moller and that the money should be repaid, an EU source said on Monday.

The European Union executive had investigated about 60 cases of aid in the Danish shipbuilding sector and found that EU aid limits had been exceeded in five cases, all of them to the Odense shipyard, the source said.
But it was not a question of large amounts of money which would need to be repaid -- about one million Danish crowns ($160,000) plus interest.
The Commission said in July it was starting a probe into Danish shipbuilding aid, fearing that subsidies might have exceeded EU limits between 1987 and 1993.
The investigation was launched following the publication of a critical independent study accusing the government of illegalities.

The study, commissioned by the Danish industry ministry and carried out by accountancy firm Coopers & Lybrand, criticised Danish ministers for subsidising the sector to the tune of four billion crowns ($636 million) over the last decade.
The Commission said then there were indications that in 65 cases vessels were financed on the basis of an inflated price level, creating a risk that the EU aid ceiling had been exceeded.
However, in September Danish Industry Minister Mimi Jacobsen presented a ministry report concluding that the administration of shipbuilding aid from 1986 to 1995 complied with EU rules.
Jacobsen, who resigned in December in a government reshuffle, said she was dropping a planned legal probe into shipbuilding aid, rejecting the findings of the Coopers & Lybrand study.

She said her ministry had studied 308 cases of aid granted to Danish shipyards and found that the report's critical stance was full of errors and misinterpretations of EU rules. Despite this, the Commission said it would complete its probe.
